ideas.title: Kingfisher Clarkfork true rotary vise (his main want, best version) <cite index="1-1">(tested)</cite>
ideas.search: Kingfisher Fly Fishing Clarkfork True Rotary Fly Tying Vise Gold
ideas.why: This is the one over-budget pick, at about 7% over, and it is my top choice for his stated need. <cite index="1-9">One review roundup calls it the smoothest true rotary under $100. It has dual ball-bearing housings and hardened tool-steel jaws that hold sizes 26 to 4/0 and grip tiny hooks firmly.</cite> That covers his size 18-and-smaller requirement for trout dry flies. It replaces the worn-out vise, so he isn't getting a duplicate. Check the shipped total at checkout, because the 15% allowance caps it at about $86.

ideas.title: Maxcatch rotary fly-tying vise with travel case <cite index="1-1">(tested)</cite>
ideas.search: Maxcatch Rotary Fly Tying Vise Alloy Travel Vise
ideas.why: This is the in-budget vise option. <cite index="1-14">It is a full rotary with adjustable tension and hardened steel jaws rated for sizes 28 to 4/0. It comes in a snap-shut case with foam holders.</cite> The jaw range easily covers size 18 and smaller. The compact case suits someone who dislikes clutter, and it could go with him on Upper Delaware trips. Confirm the price on the Amazon listing before buying, since I couldn't verify it.
